name: NAIRA GALLI · नायरा गल्ली
one_line: Twelve perfectly symmetrical pastel shopfronts on one lane, Bombay Deco drawn in Naira's own inks: every post is one shop whose rolling shutter goes up on a single real Naira piece, every row of the grid is one stretch of the same street at one hour of the day, and the profile itself becomes the lane.
big_idea:
Every woman who buys from Naira grew up on a galli: the fancy store with earrings pinned to cards, the bangle shop with its soap and its squeeze, the post office where the money order always said buy something nice, the bartan bhandar on Dhanteras, the electricals shop strung with ladis, the optician's chart, the general store's glass jars, the co-op bank with its pen on a chain, the wedding-card press, the phoolwala, the photo studio. NAIRA GALLI builds that lane once, beautifully: a Wes Anderson-level symmetrical elevation of Indian shopfronts in Naira's palette, Bombay Deco parapets (Mumbai's own premium architecture, pastel and symmetrical by nature, so the register comes from India rather than being laid on it), enamel signboards in Velista with one Marathi line under each, a curt hand-painted pati on every shop in the voice of Pune's famous shop signs, and in every window the one thing that is not drawn: a real, photographed Naira piece standing in for that shop's own goods. The joke on every tile is something that shop truly does (the bangle-wala needs soap; this bangle slips over the hand), the piece is the punchline, and one exact fact from the listing is the proof.

Three devices make it a system rather than twelve illustrations. (1) THE SHUTTER. The rolling shutter is the most familiar motion in Indian life, it already has a sound (the morning rattle), and it is a reveal. Every reel opens by rolling a shutter up and ends by rolling it down, and the closed shutter is the end card, painted with the piece, the price and the address; because every reel starts and ends on that same painted shutter, every loop is seamless. (2) THE STREET IN THE GRID. Each row of three tiles shares one sky and one pavement, drawn as a single 3,240-px strip, so at 391x521 each row reads as one continuous street. Each row is a different hour (dawn, Diwali dusk, after four, wedding night), so the grid stacks into four bands of light that alternate pale and dark, while the shopfronts alternate pale and deep in a checkerboard that continues the live LAC / flower / BONE row underneath. The bottom row's road is painted in LAC's own oxblood, so the old launch row becomes the lane's foundation. (3) THE PLATE. A municipal street-name plate re-inked in sage and cream, नायरा गल्ली over NAIRA GALLI with a shop number, stands on its post at the same coordinates on every cover and every end card: the season's lockup, as fixed as PTAT's MILNI.

The four weeks are four series named for the hour: SHUTTERS UP (the lane reopens after a long lunch; Karwa Chauth; the Diwali list), LAMPS LIT (Bhaubeej by post, Dhanteras, Diwali), AFTER FOUR (Pune's shops reopen at four: the optician, Children's Day at the general store, the bank) and OPEN LATE (the card press, Tulsi Vivah at the phoolwala, the stage photo). A stranger's three-second read: 'a street of little Indian shops, and every shop is selling one Naira piece.'
why_better_than_A_and_B:
A is NAIRA MATCHING CENTRE (245/300, one shop: a counter of fabric shades) and B is MANGAL (225/300, one house: Mummy's objects under a multi-script seal). NAIRA GALLI is built to beat both on the points the three judges marked down, and to stay out of their territory.
1. A world that contains both of theirs. A is one institution and B is one household; the galli is the whole neighbourhood those two live in, and it can hold a dozen institutions without repeating a device. Its loudest words in the grid are the shop names themselves (BANGLE CENTRE, POST OFFICE, OPTICIANS, PHOTO STUDIO), which name the world at 36% the way MILNI does.
2. The grid is the artwork. A and B both checkerboard their grounds over LAC / flower / BONE. The galli does that too, and adds two layers neither has: every row is one continuous street (shared sky, pavement, kerb, ladi lights), and the four rows are four hours of light that alternate pale and dark. Every row has one dense, one mid and one breathing shopfront by construction, which the judges asked of both.
3. Motion-first, as the owner asked. A has 2 reels and 4 statics; B has 3 reels and 3 statics. Here all 12 move: 5 reels and 7 carousels whose first slide is a seamless video loop that reads as a still in the grid, plus 18 short video slides. The motion is native to each shop (shutters, tube lights, the post-office stamp, the press's clack and metal sorts, the optician's chart lighting row by row, the bank's pen swinging on its chain, the photo studio's flash, ladis switching on), and all of it is paced to the owner's own numbers (nothing faster than 0.6 s except a stamp and a type sort).
4. A fixed lockup that carries the name. A's tag needed a must-fix to stop wandering; B's seal needed one to absorb its second wordmark. The street plate is 360x180 at the same coordinates on all 12 covers and every end card (130x65 in the grid) and puts NAIRA in two scripts on every tile; the real wordmark appears once, on the house's own board (P1) and on every end card.
5. Lower risk than either. One Devanagari line per sign (B needs ten languages and readers for each); no Kalam, no added script faces beyond Tiro Devanagari Marathi; no faces; no service promise to staff (A's WhatsApp matching counter depends on owner sign-off); no product-free tile; gift posts land in time to deliver (the earring cards on 1 Nov, Bhaubeej on 3 Nov); zero water, tarnish or hypoallergenic claims on any image; 'gold' never stands alone, and the Dhanteras shop says outright that gold coins are not sold here.
6. Different pieces doing different jobs. Where A and B both open on the Ruby bracelet (the data says so, and so does this), the rest of the run avoids their idea-and-piece pairs (A's chalni and Serpentine, the sample blouse, Duo Link for the brother, Woven 'is it gold', the Prism kandil, the four-shade huggies reel, the 36 cm necklace, the Nocturne trial room, the tulsi tile, the ruby bill; B's chalni and Droplet, the locker and Woven, the thali, the rangoli Prism, the ruby dabba, the Heartbead lifafa, the missed-call huggies, Name: Mummy, the good box, the first card, the antarpat). It gives hero slots to stock neither option leads with: Kiss Knot Bangle (40, 0 sold), North Star Bangle, Rivière Eternal Bracelet (34, 1 sold), Fine Tennis Bracelet (20, 0 sold), Silk Mesh Cuff (40, 0 sold), Toggle Link Chain (79), Mint Pear and Bold Nocturne Drops, and the Crystal baguette family. It absorbs the best insights of all four candidates in new settings: the owner's lines ('Not fashion jewellery. Not fine.', 'Look closer'), the honest Dhanteras answer, forwarding to the brother, true-scale proof (actual size printed on the earring cards, 2.5 mm on the optician's last line), the Prism-as-candy wink and a closing basket for the set.
why_it_fits:
BRAND: everything drawn uses Naira's existing palette families (identity sage, blush and ivory; the Lilac, Sage and Apricot edition grounds; the Red Room oxblood; the exhibition bottle green; the LAC oxblood sampled from the live grid; ad marigold exactly once). Signs have sharp corners; type is Velista caps with a lowercase Cormorant turn and Jost for facts and prices; the real wordmark appears only on the house's board and on end cards; the jewellery is always the real photographed piece, never drawn and never generated. The voice is the owner's caption system: one deadpan Indian line, one exact fact, the [ piece · material · wink ] kicker, no dashes, no exclamation marks, no emoji, no urgency. Festive cues are carried by the shops themselves (the electricals shop is where Diwali ladis are bought; the post office is where Bhaubeej money orders went; the phoolwala stacks sugarcane for Tulsi Vivah), never as wallpaper, and no tile carries two idioms.
DATA: (a) The account's best ad pairs one piece with one everyday Indian object and one witty line ('Anaar, pre-peeled.', ₹335 per purchase, ROAS 4.52), and concept statics beat plain ones 1.44x to 0.57x ROAS; every shop is that formula with the object scaled up to an institution. (b) Women 35 to 54 made 64% of purchases: these are the shops of their childhood (the money order and the one-to-four lunch are their memories, not Gen Z's). Maharashtra is 46% of orders, with Mumbai and Nashik leading, hence Marathi boards, Bombay Deco and Pune's shop signs. (c) Ruby is the hero stone and opens the season; the four deep-stock bestsellers each get a hero slot (Woven Gold Hoops 63 on the fancy-store card, Prism Rivière 67 in the jar, Baguette Tennis Bracelet 57 in the window, Heartbead 25 on the steel shelf), and the largest unsold lines get their first ever hero tiles (Baguette Tennis Necklace 70/0, Toggle Link Chain 79/5, Kiss Knot Bangle 40/0, Silk Mesh Cuff 40/0, Rivière Eternal 34/1, Fine Tennis 20/0). (d) Feed and Stories stills sold 84% of attributed purchases while reels bought reach, so the motion is split: 5 reels for the relaunch and reach, 7 carousels whose cover is a calm loop that reads as a still, with facts and prices on still slides inside. (e) 'Finished to be seen up close' beat 'daily wear' 3.8 to 2.2 ATC per ₹1,000 and physical proof won ('THE WIDTH.'), so every post carries one measured fact, and three posts are built on proof (actual size on the cards, 2.5 mm on the chart, true-scale rulers). (f) Sunday is the biggest order day and 12:00 to 21:00 carries 78% of orders, so posts land Sun 12:00 and weekday 18:00 to 19:00. (g) The two topics that ever broke out on the account were process and packaging: the galli shows the making of ordinary things (a stamp, a press, a sizing cone) and every end card promises the Naira box. (h) PTAT depth: a nameable world, one lockup in one place, named series, illustration framing real photographs, Indian everyday institutions as stages, colour fields that own each tile, and reel covers designed into the grid.
motion_language: HOUSE RULES OF MOVEMENT. PACE: the lane moves at walking pace, matched to the owner's own tuning (the box turns once in 35 s, the flower once in 10 s). No move is faster than 0.6 s except a rubber stamp and a type sort, which are diegetic. CAMERA: locked, frontal, orthographic, eye level, like an architect's elevation. It may only push in, pull back, truck sideways along a row strip, or pedestal straight down inside a shop, always on E-INOUT over 1.2 to 2.4 s. No tilts, no handheld drift, no whip pans, no zoom blur, no frame rotation. EASING: E-OUT (arrivals and openings: shutters up, type) cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), the site's own reveal curve. E-INOUT (camera, slides, shutters down, swaps) cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1). E-SINE (anything hanging: pati, cards, ladis, toran, chains) cubic-bezier(0.37,0,0.63,1) with alternate direction. E-DROP (an object set down: stamp, cuff, bangle) cubic-bezier(0.33,0,0.67,1), then exactly one settle swing of at most 2 degrees over 0.6 s; never a bounce. LINEAR for constant motion (clock steps, falling petals, the ceiling fan). RECURRING TRANSITIONS: SHUTTER UP, 1.6 to 1.8 s, E-OUT: the slatted shutter translates up into its box, clipped at the box's lower edge, its bottom bar casting a 0.15 s lagging shadow; sound is the rattle. TUBE ON, 0.6 s: opacity keyframes 0, 0.7 at 12%, 0.15 at 18%, 0.85 at 30%, 0.3 at 36%, 1 from 50%; exactly two soft blinks, then steady for the rest of the piece. PUSH-IN and PULL-BACK, 1.2 to 2.4 s, scale the whole scene group only. TRUCK, 2.4 s along a 3,240-px row strip. GLINT, 1.0 to 1.2 s: a 120-px soft white band at 25 degrees travelling across a piece, masked by the cut-out's own alpha, screen at 55%, at most once per 6 s. SWAP between colour or metal variants: a 0.6 s slide or a 0.4 s cross-fade, then a 0.4 to 0.6 s hold. SHUTTER DOWN, 1.0 to 1.4 s, E-INOUT, no bounce, ending on the painted end card. AMBIENT LOOPS: pati and toran sway plus or minus 1.2 to 1.5 degrees on a 4 s period; hanging cards plus or minus 1.2 to 1.8 degrees on 4 s; ladi bulbs breathe 0.8 to 1 opacity in a travelling wave with a 3 s or 4 s period; diya flames scaleY 0.94 to 1.06, out of phase and never in unison, on cycles chosen to divide the loop (0.8, 1.0 and 1.6 s in 8 s loops; 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 s in 12 s loops; 1.0, 1.25 and 1.5 s in 15 s loops); petals fall over 8 s with plus or minus 40 px sideways sway; the ceiling fan turns once per 8 s; the bank's pen swings on its bead chain on 4 s. LOOP LOGIC: every reel except P1 starts on its own painted end-card shutter and ends on the identical frame, so Instagram's replay is seamless. Every carousel's first slide is a video loop of 6 to 8 s whose frame 0 is the designed cover and whose ambient periods divide the loop length (3, 4, 6 or 8 s), so it has no seam and the grid shows the cover. TYPE: set type never moves once it has landed. It enters with opacity 0 to 1 plus a 16 px rise over 0.6 s (E-OUT), lines staggered 60 ms. The only letter-by-letter motion is diegetic: the money-order form written stroke by stroke in Cormorant italic, the press's metal sorts, the optician's chart rows lighting up. WHAT NEVER MOVES: the street plate (the camera may pass it, the plate never animates); the NAIRA wordmark; the signboards; the roofline and kerb datums, which are each row's horizon; and the jewellery's shape. Pieces only translate, or rotate up to 3 degrees about a real hanging point. They never scale-pulse, squash, warp, spin in 3D or get a cartoon sparkle star, and they are enlarged only by camera moves on the whole scene or inside a loupe marked '(shown larger.)'. LIGHT: changes take 0.8 to 1.2 s; flashes peak at 0.55 opacity and last under 0.5 s, never a strobe; every glow is warm (#E7C27A), never blue-white. FRAMING: in reels every product beat is framed with the piece between y 700 and y 1250 of the 1920 frame, and every in-video word sits between y 300 and y 1250, left of x 860 below y 1150, clear of the Reels caption and action rail; covers are separate designed stills. Renders: 30 fps via tools/reel.cjs (H.264 High, +faststart); carousel video slides render the same way at 1080x1440 with the viewport changed.

grid_system.type_system: Four faces, three of them the brand's own. VELISTA 400 (caps only; glyphs A-Z, 0-9 and . , ; : ! ? & ' " - ( ) @ # % / only): shop names on signboards 104-120 px (about 38-43 px in the grid, the words that read at 36%), pati headlines 50-64 px, end-card piece names 72-76 px, plate 'NAIRA GALLI' 50 px. Never ₹, never the middot, never °, never accented letters: 'PRISM RIVIÈRE' and 'RIVIÈRE ETERNAL' are set in Jost 500 caps wherever they appear on an image. CORMORANT GARAMOND ITALIC 400 (lowercase): the turn under every pati headline, 32-40 px, and the money-order handwriting (converted to outlines and drawn with stroke-dashoffset in graphite), never presented as anyone's real hand. JOST: 300 for facts and support lines 26-34 px, 400 for prices 40-72 px with ₹ falling back to Poppins (tokens.css --nf-font-label), 500 caps tracked 0.2-0.3 em for labels, the plate strip and card print, 12-30 px. TIRO DEVANAGARI MARATHI 400: exactly one Indian-script line per signboard (56-64 px), the plate's first line (46 px), and three short lines inside slides (the stamp's भाऊबीज, P5's honest pati, the series words); owner sign-off required as a feed face; every string checked by a Marathi reader on the final PNG. No Kalam, no Rozha, no Yatra, no fourth Latin face. Hierarchy per cover, top to bottom: signboard (shop name + script), pati (headline + turn), the piece, the plate. Never more than these four text groups on a cover.

Four screw heads (r 6) at (20,20), (340,20), (20,160), (340,160), gold #C99A4C with a 1 px #80612A slot at 30 degrees. Strip: a cream band x 13-347, y 132-167, carrying Jost 500 18 px sage deep tracked 0.16 em, centred: 'N° 01 · SHUTTERS UP' (the shop number is the post number; the series word changes by row: SHUTTERS UP, LAMPS LIT, AFTER FOUR, OPEN LATE). Post: 10 px wide #2E4238 rod from the plate's bottom edge to the footpath, with 10 x 6 px gold-deep #B0843A collars at top and foot and a soft contact shadow ellipse (60 x 8, #1A1614 at 18%). In the grid it is 130 x 65 px: the green plate with cream type reads as the season's mark even where its words do not. It never animates; it is the one thing on the lane that is nailed down.
grid_system.lockup: Two parts, used the same way on every tile. THE PLATE (C-PLATE, above) is the season lockup and the brand's name on every cover and end card, in type, as a street name. THE SIGNBOARD (C-BOARD) is each shop's name: a 920 x 230 enamel board at x 80-1000, y 330-560 (tile coordinates; reels y 570-800), sharp corners, a 6 px border in the shop's dark colour, the shop name in Velista 104-120 px centred with its baseline at y 455, and one Tiro Devanagari Marathi line (56-64 px) centred at baseline y 535. The real NAIRA wordmark (kit SVG, never retyped) sits only on N° 01's board and at the top of every end card's painted shutter, so it is never twice in one frame. Under every board hangs THE PATI (C-PATI): a cream enamel notice, 540 x 140 px (or up to 760 x 190 px for two-line headlines), centred at x 540, its top at y 590, hung on two 2 px gold chains from the board's bottom edge; Velista headline in ink (or the shop's deep colour), Cormorant italic turn in graphite. The pati is Pune's curt shop sign turned honest: every one states a true thing about the piece.

Back after lunch. In Pune the shops close from one to four. Ours closed from August to today.
The shutters on Naira Galli go up from today, one shop a post, three a week, until the first muhurat. Also in crystal and in green cubic zirconia, ₹1,699.
The listing's own tip is to wear two colours together, ruby with crystal. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off, with codes BUY2 and BUY3 at checkout.

posts.concept: In Karwa Chauth week the bangle shop is the busiest counter on the lane, and every woman remembers the ritual: the bangle-wala soaps your hand, folds your fingers, squeezes, sometimes slips a plastic bag over the knuckles, and the glass goes on with a wince. So N° 02 is a bottle-green bangle shop whose doorway is lined with poles of drawn glass bangles in Karwa Chauth red and green, a pink bar of soap sitting in a steel dish that nobody will need, and the two Kiss Knot bangles (18k gold tone and rhodium) stacked on the counter. The morning sky above it still holds a pale moon: on Karwa Chauth morning, last night's moon really is still up in the west, so the women who will wait for tonight's moon can already see one.
